name: Magistra GLP-1 Aggregate Pooled Side Effect Rates
description: Per-effect summary table only: pooled clinical rate estimate (with 95% CI, stated rates, distinct sources) and community reporting frequency (mentions, distinct reports) for each of the 15 tracked GLP-1 side effects. Computed from Magistra's underlying point-level corpus, which is NOT included here and remains under a separate attribution/no-redistribution licence (see licenseUrl). This summary table may be redistributed with attribution. Figures are pulled live from https://magistra.health/api/data?q=overview at build time — never hand-typed.
licenseNote: This aggregate table (effect, pooled rate, CI, n, distinct sources) is CC BY 4.0 — free to redistribute with attribution (Magistra, magistra.health). The underlying point-level corpus is NOT covered by this licence; see https://magistra.health/en/data#licence.
citation: Magistra Health. "GLP-1 Aggregate Pooled Side Effect Rates." magistra.health/data/glp1-aggregate-rates.json. Accessed 2026-09-12.
methodologyNote: clinicalPooledRatePct/CI: weighted random-effects pooled rate across eligible clinical + regulatory rate points, one entry per distinct source (src/lib/side-effects-engine.ts::pooledClinicalEstimate, exposed live at /api/data?q=overview -> effectsTracked[].corpusClinical). Null when the corpus has zero eligible clinical rate points for that effect. communityReportingFrequencyPct: of N distinct community reports (corpus-wide, deduped by URL), the share mentioning this effect — NOT an incidence rate, see /en/methodology (src/lib/rate-base.ts::buildReportingFrequency). clinicalIntervalBasis: "sampling_plus_between_study" normally; "sampling_only_single_source" when a single source entry contributes, in which case the between-study heterogeneity term is 0 by construction and the two CI columns describe that one study's sampling only — never read such a row's narrow interval as stronger evidence than a wider one. clinicalRateKind: "incidence" for an ordinary all-cause pooled rate; "serious_ae_floor" when every source behind the pooled rate is a rate from a trial registry’s SERIOUS adverse-events table (the registry lists non-serious events only above the trial’s reporting threshold, so such a figure is a FLOOR on all-cause incidence, not incidence); "mixed_incidence_and_serious_ae" when the pool contains both. Do not compare a serious_ae_floor row to a label’s all-cause figure without saying so.
disclaimer: Data, not medical advice. Reporting frequency is not incidence — do not compare it to the clinical rate as if the two measured the same thing.

evidentiaryBase.note: Both corpusPoints and totalDataPoints are scoped to the 15 publicly-tracked effects (excluding kidney_issues/muscle_loss/weight_regain, extraction-only categories never displayed on the site); they differ only in that corpusPoints includes the April-2026 seed points retained for audit trail and totalDataPoints excludes them. Corrected 2026-09-11: until then totalDataPoints and dataPointsBySource were computed from an unscoped metadata blob, so this response published a corpus total 97 higher than the sum of its own dataPointsByEffect — totalDataPoints read 1,901 where the scoped figure is 1,804. Of the corpus, only ratePoints state a rate; after eligibility rules, eligibleRates are allowed to support a published estimate. distinctSources counts distinct STUDIES by source URL with its fragment stripped (a registry record or paper counts once however many effects it reports; re-keyed 2026-09-08 — until then this field counted one entry per source per effect, now exposed as sourceEntries). Per-effect breakdown: ?q=effect&id=<effect>, field rateBase, whose distinctSources is keyed the same way (re-keyed 2026-09-10 — it too counted one entry per source per effect until then, and still does under sourceEntries; the two differ only where one study posts more than one MedDRA preferred term for the same effect, e.g. SURMOUNT-1's Pancreatitis and Pancreatitis acute).

knownDefect: Known upward bias, not yet corrected: registry rows collected before 2026-09-10 through the rotation path were capped at the five highest-percentage arm rows per trial, which selects on the rate being measured. 19 of the 25 trials with stored registry rows are affected; the six pinned pivotal trials (SURMOUNT-1, SELECT, STEP 1, STEP 2, SURPASS-CVOT, retatrutide phase 2) are not, because they emit every non-placebo arm. Pooled clinical estimates that draw on an affected trial therefore read HIGH by an amount we have not yet quantified per effect. The collector was fixed 2026-09-10; the stored rows await a re-collection. Method and per-trial measurements: §4 Limitations and correction-log item 25 of the published methodology, https://github.com/saurabhgoyal75/magistra-predictor/blob/main/preprint/magistra-methodology.md.
